identity.name: Pico Trust
identity.value_proposition: Hide short trust signals inside ordinary images so they survive re-sharing.
identity.target_users: Journalists and fact-checkers who publish photos and need provenance to travel with them.

requirements.text: A user can embed a signed trust payload into an image.
requirements.acceptance: Given a PNG and a payload, when the user embeds it, then the returned image decodes back to the same payload.

requirements.text: A user can verify an image from the browser.
requirements.acceptance: Given an embedded image, when the user opens it in the web app, then the app shows the payload and whether it is intact.

components.name: api
components.responsibility: Embeds and verifies trust payloads in images.

components.name: web
components.responsibility: Lets users verify an image in the browser.

glossary.meaning: The signed trust data hidden in an image.
A payload whose signature still verifies.

security.auth: API keys for publishers; verification is public.

components.name: web
components.checks: axe in the end-to-end tests, plus keyboard-only runs of R2

overrides.reason: The api is a single-process prototype; structured logs are enough until it is deployed beyond one host.

decisions.title: Product identity
decisions.context: The project needed a name, audience and testable requirements before any code.
decisions.decision: Pico Trust targets journalists, with two acceptance-tested requirements.
decisions.consequences: Features outside R1 and R2 need a new requirement first.

decisions.title: Python api plus TypeScript web
decisions.context: Image processing is easiest in Python; verification needs a browser UI.
decisions.decision: A monorepo with an api (python) and a web (typescript) component.
decisions.consequences: Two toolchains to maintain; the api contract is the integration point.

decisions.title: The web app calls the api through OpenAPI
decisions.decision: api embeds and verifies; web calls it; api/openapi.yaml is the contract.
decisions.consequences: Contract changes are reviewed as risky.

decisions.title: Problem details and user messages
decisions.context: Errors reach both API callers and browser users.
decisions.decision: api answers with problem+json; web shows messages that say how to fix the problem.
decisions.consequences: Every error names its category and a fix.

decisions.title: Unit, integration, contract and end-to-end tests
decisions.context: The api has real logic; the web app is the user's path.
decisions.decision: api: unit, integration, contract; web: unit, end-to-end.
decisions.consequences: Tests name the requirement they cover.

decisions.title: shadcn/ui on one tokens file
decisions.context: The web UI needs a consistent look without a designer on hand.
decisions.decision: web builds on shadcn/ui, with every color, space and font in web/src/styles/tokens.css.
decisions.consequences: Ad-hoc styles outside the tokens are review findings; screenshots catch visual regressions.

decisions.title: User guide in docs/guide
decisions.context: Users need a guide to the web app and the public API.
decisions.decision: External docs live in docs/guide; api routes and web pages map to it.
decisions.consequences: A change to a route or page must update the guide.

decisions.title: GitHub Actions, container api, static web
decisions.context: Both components are deployed to staging and production.
decisions.decision: CI on GitHub Actions; api as a container on Fly.io, web on Cloudflare Pages.
decisions.consequences: Every push runs both components' checks; hosting is documented, not provisioned.

decisions.title: Secrets in Fly.io, API keys for publishers
decisions.context: The api signs payloads with keys that must never leak.
decisions.decision: Production secrets live in Fly.io secrets; publishers authenticate with API keys; api/keys/** is protected.

decisions.title: Weekly Dependabot updates
decisions.context: Two toolchains and pinned CI actions drift.
decisions.decision: Dependabot opens weekly update pull requests per component and for the CI actions.
decisions.consequences: Each update runs CI before it merges.

decisions.title: JSON logs correlated by traceparent
decisions.context: A browser request spans web and api.
decisions.decision: Both components log JSON and pass the W3C traceparent.
decisions.consequences: One request can be followed across components.

decisions.title: WCAG 2.2 AA
decisions.context: Public users include keyboard and screen reader users.
decisions.decision: web targets WCAG 2.2 AA, checked by axe in the end-to-end tests.
decisions.consequences: An axe violation fails the end-to-end tests.

decisions.title: Conventional commits on trunk
decisions.context: A solo maintainer with agents committing needs a predictable history.
decisions.decision: Conventional commits scoped by component, committed straight to trunk.
decisions.consequences: The commit-msg hook rejects messages that break the convention.

decisions.title: Batched review
decisions.context: Reviewing every task is slow; unreviewed large diffs are risky.
decisions.decision: Batched review with a 200 line / 5 file threshold.
decisions.consequences: Agents stop for review once a batch crosses either limit.
